titel: Kurt Andersen Has a New Book Out (and it's amazing)

einzeiler: Kurt Andersen discusses his new novel, the future of America, and writing in 2045.
kurzfassung: Kurt Andersen discusses his speculative novel 'The Breakup', which is set in a fractured America in the year 2045. He and Alec Baldwin explore the parallels between his fictional civil war and current political polarization. Andersen also shares insights into his writing process, research habits, and evolving view of artificial intelligence.
stichpunkte: Kurt Andersen's novel 'The Breakup' is set in 2045 and follows a separated couple amid a divided America.
The book features flashbacks to a second American civil war that took place in the late 2030s.
Andersen began writing the book in 2022 before the rapid rise of AI and subsequent political developments.
The conversation covers Donald Trump's political career, the second term, and the rise of right-wing political movements.
Andersen explains how writing novels differs from screenplays because characters take on lives of their own.
He humorously notes that he recently started using AI tools like Claude to check vocabulary and alternatives.
Andersen maintains a temperamentally 51 percent optimistic outlook despite the darker themes in his recent work.

beschreibung:
Kurt Andersen has spent four decades chronicling America’s culture and politics in both fiction and nonfiction. In 1986, Andersen co-founded Spy Magazine, which became a cultural zeitgeist and influenced a generation of journalists. Andersen then co-created and hosted Studio 360, a Peabody Award-winning public radio show and podcast about art and pop culture which aired from 2000 to 2020. He is also a former editor-in-chief of New York magazine, columnist and staff writer for the New Yorker, Time magazine critic and columnist, and has written for television, film, and the stage. Andersen appears regularly as a commentator on MSNOW, and continues to contribute to The Atlantic and the New York Times. In addition to his work in print media, Kurt Andersen is the author of the New York Times bestsellers Evil Geniuses: The Unmaking of America, A Recent History and Fantasyland: How America Went Haywire, A 500-Year History, as well as the bestselling novels You Can’t Spell America Without Me, True Believers, Heyday, and Turn of the Century.
